title: The Appointment That Was Hard to Keep
title_ja: 通院の予約を守ることが難しい理由
fact_notes: 健康の社会的要因に関するWHO資料を参照。通院の事例は架空で医学的助言を意図しない。
本文・訳・設問・解説はオリジナル。

sentences.en: A clinic notices that some patients miss appointments even when they say they want medical advice.
sentences.ja: ある診療所では、医療的な助言を求めていると言う患者でも予約を逃すことがあると気づきます。

sentences.en: At first, a staff member suggests that the patients simply do not care enough about their health.
sentences.ja: 最初、職員の一人は患者たちが健康を十分に大切にしていないだけだと考えます。

sentences.en: However, another worker asks whether the appointment times are possible for everyone who needs care.
sentences.ja: しかし別の職員は、診療が必要なすべての人にその予約時刻が可能なのかと尋ねます。

sentences.en: A patient may depend on a bus that runs infrequently, while another may be unable to leave work without losing pay.
sentences.ja: 患者の一人は便数の少ないバスに頼り、別の人は給料を失わずに仕事を抜けられないかもしれません。

sentences.en: A parent may also need someone to watch a young child before traveling to the clinic.
sentences.ja: 親なら診療所へ行く前に幼い子を見守る人が必要かもしれません。

sentences.en: These examples suggest that a missed appointment does not always reveal a person's motivation.
sentences.ja: こうした例は予約を逃したことが必ずしも本人の意欲を示すわけではないと示します。

sentences.en: The World Health Organization describes social determinants of health as conditions in which people are born, grow, live, work, and age.
sentences.ja: 世界保健機関は健康の社会的要因を、人が生まれ、育ち、暮らし、働き、年を重ねる条件として説明します。

sentences.en: These conditions include access to resources and opportunities that shape everyday choices.
sentences.ja: その条件には日常の選択を形作る資源や機会へのアクセスが含まれます。

sentences.en: For example, two patients may receive the same written instructions but have very different ways of reaching a medical service.
sentences.ja: 例えば二人の患者が同じ書面の指示を受けても、医療サービスへの到達方法は大きく異なるかもしれません。

sentences.en: One person may travel quickly by car, whereas another must coordinate several forms of public transport.
sentences.ja: 一人は車ですぐ行けても、もう一人は複数の公共交通機関を調整しなければならないかもしれません。

sentences.en: Providing identical information does not necessarily create equal opportunities to act on it.
sentences.ja: 同一の情報を提供しても、それを実行する機会が平等に生まれるとは限りません。

sentences.en: Understanding access therefore requires attention to the practical circumstances beyond the clinic itself.
sentences.ja: したがってアクセスの理解には、診療所の外にある実際の事情への注意が必要です。

sentences.en: The clinic begins by asking patients which parts of the appointment process are most difficult for them.
sentences.ja: 診療所は予約過程のどの部分が最も難しいか患者に尋ねることから始めます。

sentences.en: Some describe long journeys, while others mention schedules that change unexpectedly at work.
sentences.ja: 長い移動を挙げる人もいれば、職場で予定が突然変わることを挙げる人もいます。

sentences.en: Instead of treating all answers as proof of the same problem, staff organize the concerns into different categories.
sentences.ja: すべての回答を同じ問題の証拠とみなすのではなく、職員は懸念を異なる分類に整理します。

sentences.en: They also recognize that people may hesitate to describe financial or family difficulties to strangers.
sentences.ja: また、金銭や家庭の困難を見知らぬ人に話すことをためらう人がいると認識します。

sentences.en: The clinic therefore avoids demanding unnecessary personal details simply to offer general information about available services.
sentences.ja: そのため利用可能なサービスについて一般的な情報を提供するだけのために、不必要な個人情報を求めないようにします。

sentences.en: Listening carefully can improve service design without assuming that every patient has the same needs.
sentences.ja: 丁寧に聞くことは、すべての患者が同じ必要を持つと決めつけずにサービス設計を改善できます。

sentences.en: Several possible changes are discussed, including clearer directions, reminders, and information about different appointment options.
sentences.ja: より明確な道順、通知、異なる予約方法の案内など、いくつかの変更案が話し合われます。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, each option has limits that should be considered before it becomes a permanent policy.
sentences.ja: それでも各案には恒久的な方針にする前に考慮すべき限界があります。

sentences.en: A reminder cannot create a bus route that does not exist, and a different appointment time may not solve unpredictable work schedules.
sentences.ja: 通知は存在しないバス路線を作れず、別の予約時刻でも予測できない勤務予定は解決しないかもしれません。

sentences.en: The staff decide to test a small set of changes and ask patients whether those changes make appointments more practical.
sentences.ja: 職員たちは少数の変更を試し、その変更で予約がより実用的になったか患者に尋ねることにします。

sentences.en: They compare missed appointments before and after the trial but avoid assuming that any change in the numbers has only one cause.
sentences.ja: 試行前後の予約欠席を比較しますが、数字の変化に原因が一つしかないと決めつけません。

sentences.en: This cautious approach recognizes that service improvement depends on evidence as well as good intentions.
sentences.ja: この慎重な方法はサービス改善に善意だけでなく証拠も必要だと認めます。

sentences.en: After several weeks, some patients report that clearer travel information has made visits easier to plan.
sentences.ja: 数週間後、より明確な交通案内で受診計画が立てやすくなったと述べる患者がいます。

sentences.en: Others still face barriers outside the clinic's direct control, such as limited transport or changing employment demands.
sentences.ja: 別の人々は限られた交通手段や変わる仕事の要求など、診療所が直接管理できない障壁に直面しています。

sentences.en: As a result, the staff understand that improving access is an ongoing process rather than a single completed project.
sentences.ja: その結果、職員はアクセス改善が一度完了する事業ではなく、継続する過程だと理解します。

sentences.en: They continue to share information with community organizations while respecting the privacy and choices of individual patients.
sentences.ja: 個々の患者のプライバシーと選択を尊重しながら、地域の組織と情報を共有し続けます。

sentences.en: The experience changes how staff interpret missed appointments: they now ask which obstacles might be present before judging commitment.
sentences.ja: この経験によって予約欠席の解釈が変わり、今では意欲を判断する前にどんな障害があるか尋ねます。

sentences.en: Health services become more equitable when people can act on advice under the real conditions of their lives.
sentences.ja: 人々が実際の生活条件の下で助言に従えるとき、医療サービスはより公平になるのです。

questions.prompt: What does one staff member initially assume?
options: Patients who miss appointments do not care about health.
The clinic has no available doctors.
Every patient drives to the clinic.
Appointments are always unnecessary.
questions.explanation_ja: 第1段落「最初、職員の一人は患者たちが健康を十分に大切にしていないだけだと考えます。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: Why might a patient miss an appointment despite wanting care?
options: All patients dislike medical advice.
A written reminder always causes delays.
Every clinic is closed on weekdays.
Work or transport restrictions may prevent attendance.
questions.explanation_ja: 第1段落「患者の一人は便数の少ないバスに頼り、別の人は給料を失わずに仕事を抜けられないかもしれません。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What does WHO emphasize about health?
options: Health has no relation to available resources.
Transport cannot affect access to services.
Living and working conditions can influence health.
Only individual choices affect outcomes.
questions.explanation_ja: 第2段落「世界保健機関は健康の社会的要因を、人が生まれ、育ち、暮らし、働き、年を重ねる条件として説明します。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What does identical information fail to guarantee?
options: That all patients are given an appointment.
Equal chances to act on medical advice.
The same written instructions for everyone.
That patients receive any information.
questions.explanation_ja: 第2段落「同一の情報を提供しても、それを実行する機会が平等に生まれるとは限りません。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: How do clinic staff use patients' responses?
options: They classify different barriers instead of assuming one cause.
They reject all explanations as excuses.
They publish sensitive details publicly.
They ask everyone the same unrelated question.
questions.explanation_ja: 第3段落「すべての回答を同じ問題の証拠とみなすのではなく、職員は懸念を異なる分類に整理します。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: Why are unnecessary personal details avoided?
options: The clinic wants to stop helping patients.
All medical information is public.
Transportation details are always irrelevant.
Patients may find financial and family information sensitive.
questions.explanation_ja: 第3段落「そのため利用可能なサービスについて一般的な情報を提供するだけのために、不必要な個人情報を求めないようにします。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: Why might reminders alone be insufficient?
options: They remove every travel barrier.
They guarantee all patients will attend.
They cannot solve missing transport or unpredictable work schedules.
They automatically create more buses.
questions.explanation_ja: 第4段落「通知は存在しないバス路線を作れず、別の予約時刻でも予測できない勤務予定は解決しないかもしれません。」が根拠です。

options: Without asking any patients.
By a trial and feedback while considering other possible causes.
Only by counting how many posters are printed.
By assuming a lower number proves one exact cause.
questions.explanation_ja: 第4段落「試行前後の予約欠席を比較しますが、数字の変化に原因が一つしかないと決めつけません。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What barriers may remain outside clinic control?
options: Limited transport and changing employment demands.
The shape of every examination form.
Only the number of desks in the clinic.
The colors used in notices.
questions.explanation_ja: 第5段落「別の人々は限られた交通手段や変わる仕事の要求など、診療所が直接管理できない障壁に直面しています。」が根拠です。

questions.prompt: What is the central idea of the passage?
options: Missing an appointment always proves a lack of motivation.
One reminder permanently solves all access problems.
Every patient benefits from exactly the same schedule.
Fair health access requires attention to real-life conditions and continuing evaluation.
questions.explanation_ja: 第5段落「人々が実際の生活条件の下で助言に従えるとき、医療サービスはより公平になるのです。」が根拠です。

paraphrases.source: These examples suggest that a missed appointment does not always reveal a person's motivation.
paraphrases.rewrite: Missing an appointment may reflect barriers rather than low motivation.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 予約欠席は意欲不足だけを意味しないという趣旨です。

paraphrases.source: Providing identical information does not necessarily create equal opportunities to act on it.
paraphrases.rewrite: Giving everyone the same directions does not ensure equal access.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 同じ情報と平等な機会の違いです。

paraphrases.source: This cautious approach recognizes that service improvement depends on evidence as well as good intentions.
paraphrases.rewrite: Good intentions need to be supported by careful evaluation.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 善意と根拠を組み合わせる必要を述べます。

paraphrases.source: Health services become more equitable when people can act on advice under the real conditions of their lives.
paraphrases.rewrite: Equitable care must account for the conditions in which patients actually live.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 患者の生活条件を考慮した公平性という結論です。
